prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Every request now needs a bearer key. A missing or unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`, and a known key without the role gets 403 `forbidden`, both in the usual error shape. By default, GET routes need `viewer` and every other route needs `manager`. Four routes accept `cook`: cooking a recipe, recording waste, logging a temperature and entering stock-take counts. Every non-GET request with a known key writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status), including requests that were refused or failed. `GET /audit` is for managers and lists entries newest first. data/seed.json has one development key per role (`seed-viewer-key`, `seed-cook-key`, `seed-manager-key`). The existing tests send the manager key through tests/helpers.js, and the new tests in tests/auth.test.js cover the roles and the audit log. `npm test` (32 passing) and `npm run lint` both pass. Three things to know: (1) I did not add keys to data/db.json, the file `npm start` uses, so the server lets no one in until real keys are added there; (2) I did not bump the schema version, because `apiKeys` and `audit` are optional collections like `stocktakes` and `outbox` were; (3) after a successful change the server saves the file a second time to write the audit entry, so a crash between the two saves would lose that entry.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
